items.title: Package managers can award a package
items.description: The specification must let package managers award a supplier package to one supplier, and must say how a package manager is told apart from other users when the award action is offered and when it is carried out.
uncertainties: Whether any role other than package managers may award is not stated (REQ-001 ambiguity_notes).
Whether a package manager may award any package or only certain packages is not established.
How the product identifies users and roles is not established; no signed-in user or role is shown in the capture.

items.title: Awarded supplier must come from the attached quotes
items.description: The specification must restrict the award to a supplier chosen from the quotes attached to the package, and must say what the package manager sees if they try to award outside that rule.
uncertainties: DEC-001's recorded interpretation ('Only suppliers are eligible.') differs from its verbatim; this item follows the verbatim, as ASM-G-001 does.
What a quote contains (for example supplier and amount) is not established.
The capture shows no control for choosing the supplier (SCR-012), so how the choice is made is not established.
What happens when no quotes are attached is not decided.

items.title: One final award per package
items.description: A package is awarded to exactly one supplier and the award is final: it cannot be changed or undone by anyone. The specification must ensure that once a package is awarded, no further award attempt on it, whether repeated or made at the same time by someone else, can produce a second or different award.
uncertainties: What the user sees when their award attempt is refused because the package was already awarded is not decided.
Whether repeated supplier emails must be prevented for repeated attempts is not decided.

items.title: Awarded packages are read-only for everyone
items.description: Once awarded, a package is read-only for every user and all of its fields are locked. The specification must apply the lock to every way the package can be changed, not only to the award button, and must state that no user can lift it.
uncertainties: Whether the lock also covers the quotes attached to the package is not stated.
Which packages each user can see is not established.

items.title: Winning supplier is emailed when the award is made
items.description: The specification must send an email to the winning supplier at the time the award is made.
uncertainties: Where each supplier's email address comes from is not established; the capture shows only a supplier name.
How emails reach suppliers (which sending system, if any exists) is not established; no technical documents were supplied.

items.title: Notification recipients and email content
items.description: Whether unsuccessful quoting suppliers are also emailed, and what the award email must contain, must be decided before the notification can be specified.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-004 verbatim 'Suppliers are notified' vs interpretation 'Winning supplier'

uncertainties: DEC-004 verbatim says 'Suppliers' while its interpretation names only the winning supplier.
Email content is not stated.

items.title: Show email delivery failure to staff
items.description: If the award email cannot be delivered, the failure should be shown to staff so they can retry or contact the supplier another way. The award stays in force regardless (DEC-002).
uncertainties: The supporting source is a test fixture with low confidence and the finding is marked needs_confirmation.
Which staff are told, and how, is not established.
How delivery failure is detected is not established.

items.title: Confirm before the irreversible award
items.description: Because awards cannot be undone, a confirmation step should come before the award is committed. It should name the package and the supplier being awarded, and its confirm control should be labelled with the action (for example 'Award package') rather than a generic OK. Confirmation, not undo, applies to actions that cannot be undone.
uncertainties: All supporting sources are test fixtures with low confidence; F-GAP-005-01 is marked needs_confirmation.
Whether the confirmation should also show value, award note or quote is not covered by any source.

items.title: Outcome of pressing Award Package
items.description: What the package manager sees after pressing Award Package (in progress, success, and failure of the award itself) and the state the package is left in after a failed award must be decided. No kept finding covers this.
uncertainties: Whether success changes the status to Awarded with a recorded date, as seen on PKG-105, is not confirmed.
Whether the user stays on the package page after awarding is not shown.

new_unknowns.question: When a package is awarded, should suppliers whose quotes were not chosen also be emailed, and what must the award email(s) say?
new_unknowns.why_it_matters: Your answer 'Suppliers are notified by email when the award is made' could mean only the winner or every quoting supplier; the email cannot be specified without knowing who receives it and what it contains.

new_unknowns.question: After a package manager presses Award Package, what should they see if the award succeeds, and what if it fails?
new_unknowns.why_it_matters: Awards are final, so users need to know for certain whether an award went through; an unclear result could lead to a mistaken belief that a package was or was not awarded.

assumptions.text: A successful award moves the package to the 'Awarded' state with an award date, as shown for PKG-105 in the mockup.
assumptions.why: The captured PKG-105 page shows 'Awarded on 2 Oct 2026', but the transition itself is not shown.
assumptions.impact: FEA-009 treats the PKG-105 page as the post-award state.
assumptions.to_confirm: That awarding sets the status to Awarded and records the award date.
